items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1961-02-10
items.q: They didn't know it was Dolmott.

ctx.x: Now, Storyville. Was Storyville everything that legend says it's like?

Yeah, I think so. But they put it in a nice way. Storyville, it used to be the red light district. It was. Yeah. But for modern eyes of the jazz and things, kids couldn't pick up on that. They didn't know it was Dolmott. So they just put Storyville from the musical end of it, see? And that's where jazz began, then? Was it going to drift up the Mississippi right up to Chicago? Right up to Mississippi on the levees and the plantations and all those melodies. And that rhythm, see? And before that, come to think of…

Well, that would be about our only true American music. Yeah, that's it. They brought it there. Now, those red beans and rice we were talking about, you had plenty of that. How do you like the French cooking over here? Well, that's the same.
